introduction: An agent session records one agent run against one workspace: who opened it, with which credential, how it ended and the tokens it consumed. This package opens, closes and reads sessions, aggregates their cost, ends them with their workspace, and builds the cursor pagination every later paged route uses.

glossary.agent session: The record of one agent run against one workspace, from the credential that opened it to its terminal status and its token usage.
glossary.cursor: An opaque string identifying a position in an ordered result, issued by the service and accepted back to continue from that position.
glossary.session creator: The credential that opened a session. Only it and an admin token may complete the session or report its usage, so one agent cannot close another's.
glossary.token summary: The totals of a session's usage records, returned with the session itself.

requirements.title: Cursor pagination
requirements.rationale: Every later paged route depends on it, and a cursor that skips or repeats a row is a correctness bug a client cannot see.

criteria.action: return next_cursor and has_more with every page, where next_cursor is null exactly on the last page
criteria.contract: the page object carries {"next_cursor": <string or null>, "has_more": <boolean>}; has_more is false exactly when next_cursor is null

criteria.condition: a caller passes a page's next_cursor back as the cursor parameter
criteria.action: return the rows that follow the last row of that page, in the requested order
criteria.contract: the first row of the new page is the row immediately after the previous page's last row in the requested order

criteria.action: for any set of rows, any page size of 1 or more and either order, yield every row exactly once in the requested order when pages are read until has_more is false
criteria.contract: the concatenation of the pages equals the full ordered set, with no row repeated and none missing

criteria.condition: a cursor is malformed, truncated, or not one this service issued
criteria.action: refuse the request and return no rows
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; the response carries no page and no rows; a valid cursor still works afterwards

requirements.title: Opening a session
requirements.rationale: An agent that cannot open a session runs uncounted, and an open that is not idempotent double-counts a retried start.

criteria.condition: a session is opened against a workspace the caller may write
criteria.action: record it with its workspace, run, node, archetype, model and metadata, and answer with it
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the session carrying its id, workspace_slug, credential_id, credential_type, status active and started_at

criteria.condition: an open repeats an id that already exists and the caller may read that session's workspace
criteria.action: answer with the existing session rather than creating a second
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the existing session unchanged; no second session is recorded

criteria.action: require write access to the named workspace whatever the workspace's status
criteria.contract: the owner and an admin token may open a session on an active and on an archived workspace; a member of its organization is refused

criteria.condition: an open has no workspace_slug, names a workspace the caller may not see, or replays an id belonging to a workspace the caller may not read
criteria.action: refuse the request and record nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for a missing or empty workspace_slug and HTTP 404 "workspace not found" for the other two; no session is recorded

requirements.title: Completing a session and reporting its usage
requirements.rationale: Several agents share a workspace, so the wrong access rule here lets one agent close another's session or spend against it.

criteria.condition: the creator of an active session completes it with completed, failed or timeout
criteria.action: close it with that status and answer with it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the session at the given status; completing an already terminal session answers 200 with it unchanged

criteria.condition: the creator of an active session reports usage with a model and its token counts
criteria.action: record the usage against the session
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the usage record; the session's token summary afterwards includes these counts

criteria.action: admit the complete and usage routes only to the session's creator and to an admin token
criteria.contract: the workspace's owner, when not the session's creator, is refused; the creator and an admin token are admitted

criteria.condition: a complete has an invalid status or the status terminated, or a caller is not the session's creator, or the session does not exist, or another close of the same session is under way
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the session as it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for an invalid status and for terminated, HTTP 403 "not session owner", HTTP 404 for an unknown session and HTTP 409 for a concurrent close; the session's status is unchanged

criteria.condition: a usage report has no model, comes from a caller who is not the creator, names a session that does not exist or is not active, or carries a negative token count
criteria.action: refuse the request and record no usage
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for a missing model, HTTP 403 "not session owner", HTTP 404 for an unknown session, HTTP 409 for a session that is not active and HTTP 422 for a negative count; no usage record is written

requirements.title: Reading sessions and their usage
requirements.rationale: A total that changes with the page size is not a total, and the archived-workspace answer differs here from everywhere else.

criteria.action: return them newest first by default, each with its token summary, honouring the workspace, run, status, credential type and start-time filters, the order and the page size
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with sessions, next_cursor and has_more; the default order is newest first and the default page size 50, with 500 the maximum; each filter narrows the result to the sessions matching it

criteria.condition: one session's usage records are listed
criteria.action: return the page of records together with totals computed over every record of the session
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with records, totals, next_cursor and has_more; the default page size is 100 with 1000 the maximum; the totals are identical whatever page size is used

criteria.action: require read access and an active workspace for every session and usage read
criteria.contract: the owner, a member and an admin token read sessions of an active workspace; anyone else, and a member or owner of an archived workspace, is answered HTTP 403 "workspace access denied"

criteria.condition: a session read names a session that does not exist, or a list or usage read carries an invalid cursor
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 for an unknown session and HTTP 400 for an invalid cursor

requirements.title: Reporting a workspace's cost
requirements.rationale: This is the aggregate a person actually reads, so it has to agree with the sessions it summarises.

criteria.action: aggregate its sessions' token usage over the period, grouped by day, session or model
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the workspace, the period, the totals and a breakdown; the grouping defaults to day and the period to the last 24 hours; the totals equal the sum of the breakdown and agree with the sessions' own usage records

criteria.condition: the period's start is not before its end, or the grouping is not day, session or model
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope

criteria.condition: the cost of a workspace the caller may not read, or of an archived workspace, is requested
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 "workspace access denied", including for a member and for the owner of an archived workspace

requirements.title: Ending sessions with their workspace
requirements.rationale: A session left active on a retired workspace counts against nothing and never closes.

criteria.condition: a workspace is archived or deleted
criteria.action: end every active session of that workspace with the status terminated
criteria.contract: each formerly active session has status terminated afterwards; sessions that were already terminal are unchanged

criteria.action: leave no active session on a workspace that has been archived or deleted
criteria.contract: a listing of that workspace's sessions, by an admin token, returns none at status active

execution_paths.title: An agent run is recorded from open to completion

steps.action: opens a session against a workspace it may write
records the session with the opening credential and answers 201
reports usage twice as it works, for two different models
completes the session with completed and a duration
reads the session and finds its token summary, then lists its usage records and finds totals over both reports

execution_paths.title: A cost report is read across days and models

steps.action: runs several sessions across two days using two models, reporting usage for each
reads the workspace's cost grouped by day
aggregates the usage records over the period and answers with totals and a breakdown
reads the same cost grouped by model and finds totals that agree with the first

execution_paths.title: A workspace is archived under a running agent

steps.action: opens a session and begins working
ends the workspace's active sessions with the status terminated
reads its session and is refused 403 workspace access denied, because the workspace is no longer active
